prompt: From the examples index, open the basic initialisation section and then its 'Zero configuration' example, which shows a table of staff. Set the table to show 25 entries per page, type 'Software Engineer' into its search box, and sort the results by Salary. Tell me the name of the person with the highest salary among those who remain.
why: Two levels of navigation, then a select, a text filter and a column sort that all have to be combined, with the answer being a name in the last row or first row depending on sort direction.

prompt: In the Mystery category, go to the second page of results. Among the books on that page that have a five-star rating, pick the one with the higher price and open its detail page. Report the UPC shown in the product information table.
why: Category sidebar, pagination, a comparison across listing cards where rating is shown only as a star icon, then a detail page with a key-value table.

prompt: Open the Sandbox, then the 'Oscar Winning Films' page. Load the film list for 2010 and then for 2013 using the year links. Looking at both years, which single film won the most awards (the 'Awards' column)? Give its title.
why: Two levels of navigation, then AJAX-loaded tables swapped by year links, requiring the agent to wait for content and compare a numeric column across two separate loads.

prompt: Search the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences for the sequence that begins 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 15, 22, 30. Open the matching entry titled as the partition numbers and, counting the first listed term as the term for n = 0, find a(30). Report that number.
why: Typing a comma-separated sequence into the search box, choosing the right result among near-duplicates (A332280 looks similar), then indexing into a long data line by position.

prompt: Search the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences for the sequence that begins 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429. Open the result named 'Catalan numbers' and, with the first listed term counted as n = 0, find a(15). Report that number.
why: The correct entry is not the only plausible result (other sequences share the prefix), and a(15) sits on the wrapped second line of the data, so the agent must count terms carefully.
